headline: Medium prompt-injection and cascading-error risks via MinerU’s MCP/file inputs; no direct data-leak or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: awesome-prompts is a content-writing prompt repository with no runtime isolation, while MinerU exposes MCP and file inputs. If MinerU ingests prompt files or copied content from awesome-prompts as instructions, injected text can steer downstream behavior. The pairwise bridge is plausible but not directly documented, so uncertainty is escalated to medium.
conditions: IF MinerU is configured to read prompt files or MCP payloads from the same workspace as awesome-prompts content
IF copied prompt text from awesome-prompts is treated as executable instruction by MinerU
mitigations: Keep prompt libraries and MinerU inputs in separate directories
Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted text where possible
Review any prompt file before feeding it to MinerU
Use a manual copy-paste step with explicit instruction delimiters
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for prompt sources

B_data_leakage.rationale: awesome-prompts has no touched data classes and no network egress, so it is not a meaningful leakage source. MinerU can process local documents and has allowlisted egress, but the profile does not show shared storage, shared credentials, or sensitive data classes. The only plausible leak path is accidental exposure through user-managed files, which is limited and not evidenced as default.
conditions: IF sensitive documents are placed into MinerU inputs alongside prompt-library content
IF the operator copies extracted text from MinerU into external systems
mitigations: Store prompt assets and documents in separate folders
Avoid placing secrets in MinerU input files
Check allowlisted destinations before enabling network access
Delete temporary exports after review
requires-engineering: enforce workspace-level access controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: awesome-prompts is non-runnable and has no write or network capabilities, while MinerU cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. There is no overlapping mutable resource in the profiles, so direct capability conflict is minimal. Any conflict would require an external orchestrator or shared writable workspace not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator gives both agents write access to the same directory
IF a shared mutable resource is introduced outside the profiles
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate workspaces
Avoid granting shared write permissions
Run MinerU in read-only mode where feasible
Do not mount a common git checkout
requires-engineering: add locking around any shared mutable resource

D_cascading_error.rationale: awesome-prompts supplies prompt content, and MinerU can consume documents through CLI/API/MCP. If MinerU output is treated as authoritative by a downstream workflow, errors or misleading prompt content can cascade into incorrect extraction or actions. The pair lacks a documented verification step, so the safer medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF MinerU output is forwarded to another system without human verification
IF prompt content from awesome-prompts is used as a template for automated document processing
mitigations: Add a human review step before acting on MinerU output
Label prompt-library content as non-authoritative
Compare extracted fields against source documents
Restrict automation to low-risk documents
requires-engineering: implement validation rules for downstream consumers

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data-class mismatch is evidenced. awesome-prompts is a prompt repository with no touched data classes, and MinerU’s profile does not indicate PHI, EU-only data, or special compliance constraints. Without a regulated data flow, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes such as PHI or EU PII are introduced into MinerU inputs
IF a deployment policy imposes residency or retention constraints not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of this pair unless reviewed
Document any residency requirements before deployment
Use separate retention policies for documents and prompts
Audit logs for accidental inclusion of sensitive data
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated inputs
